data.name: The Succubi Trap
data.detailed_description:
You are trapped in a procedurally generated maze. Use your sword to spill blood and navigate the confusing hallways and corners of The Succubi Trap all the while being chased by a dual blade-wielding demon. Survive and locate the end of the maze, a chamber that is identical to the one you start in, to complete the game.

Features

* Procedurally-generated maze: Each play-through provides a maze with a unique layout. The distance between the starting chamber and end goal chamber is sufficiently large at random to avoid giving players easy escapes.

* Drain-to-trail mechanic: Spill blood to reveal the layout of the maze in adjacent tiles on the minimap and allow the distance counter next to the minimap to signal how far away you are from the end goal chamber briefly (5seconds).

*Succubi Goddess Fire Statue: Roll the dice on reaching ever so slightly closer to the end goal chamber by walking through this power-up or navigate around the confines of its boundaries to pass straight through a hallway.

reviews.review:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=lX77WokGv_o

`REVIEW KEY PROVIDED BY DEVS`

Re-Review:

The Succubi Trap is a maze game with dark elements. The character you play as weilds a sword to be able to protect themselves against the single enemy of the game, the flying demon thing. The player can swing the sword, do a forward jab, dodge (which also has an exploit) and cut themselves to spill blood on the ground to mark the ground with where you've been which also becomes marked on the minimap even though the map marking is ridiculously hard to see.

The dodge exploit allows a player to gain a ridiculous amount of speed. All I had to do was walk backwards and hit the right click to dodge forwards. If you just hold down going back and spam dodge, you will constantly just zoom through corridors.

The thing about maze games is that they're never really fun as they are never really designed well. This game is procedurally generated and has portals that will teleport you randomly around the maze. Every playthrough of this game could be shorter or longer than the last. However, maze games can be easily beat by staying to either the left or right wall while playing all the way through. However, the dev has updated the game to try to remove the ability to do so. During my two playthroughs I stayed to the right wall, finishing my first playthrough in five minutes while my second playthrough was thirty.

Within the walls of the maze are red orbs, when picked up heal the player and gives them extra life in their life bar. The player starts with 100 life, but the starting room hands the player an orb raising their health to 104. The demon within the maze does 2-3 damage per hit and attacks you around 5 times per flurry. However, this demon is easily avoidable. It is slow, then speeds up behind you to attack. When the attack animation triggers, the demon halts their movement and misses you completely if you just keep running forward. You can attack the demon if you'd like as you do a large amount of damage to it and it does little damage to you.

As this game is a project by the developer to test the human psyche, I still don't understand why the game has a pricetag. There are plenty of free games out there that are far better than this game in every way. As a game developer myself, I take pride in making games that interest all kinds of gamers. This sort of game is very niche. The devs were kind enough to send me a review key.

I just cannot recommend this game as it has too many problems and isn't interesting at all. Even through the procedural generation, all the walls and floors of the maze are the same. You look at black, grey, red and orange colors and that's about it. The demon is anoying and easily exploitable (as it can get stuck into walls and too slow to even hit the player).

This game should be free on Gamejolt or Itch.io. I don't understand why a test game, and the first of this developer, is being placed for sale for what you're getting. The psychological aspect of the game, that the devs were going for, just doesn't work.

The game lacks substance and any reason to attempt another try through the maze. Nothing about the game makes me go "I wonder what's going to happen this time..." as every playthrough is pretty much the same. This is due to the visuals and game mechanics never changing. Once you play the game and beat it once, that's all there is to see.
